full_judgment:
Md Abdur Rouf J: This appeal, following leave, by the accused-appellant is from the judgment and order dated 28-5-95 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in, Criminal Revision No.15 of 1987 discharging the Rule issued under section 561A of Code of Criminal Procedure for abashment of CR Case No.360-C of 1986 under section 420 of the Penal Code, pending in the Court of Magistrate, Bogra. 

 3. A case was registered as CR Case No.304-C/86 under section 420 of the Penal Code against the appellant. The complainant respondent No.2 having failed to appear in Court on 20-10-86, fixed for hearing of the case, the concerned Magistrate acquitted the appellant under section 247 Cr PC. Thereafter on 29-10-86, respondent No.2 on the self-same allegations lodged a second complaint before the same Magistrate against the petitioner. After recording the statement of the complainant under section 200 Cr P.C the concerned Magistrate again took cognizance of the offence under section 420 of the Penal Code and issued warrant of arrest against the appellant in CR Case No.360-C of 1986. The appellant, then moved the High Court Division under section 561A Cr P.C for quashing the said case and obtained a Rule, Criminal Revision No.15 of 1987. 

 4. A Division Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order discharged the Rule holding, inter alia, that the order of acquittal contemplated under section 247 Cr P.C is not an acquittal within the meaning of section 403 Cr P.C and as such a fresh prosecution on the alleged facts is entertainable. The learned Judges of the High Court Division have distinguished the reported case, Islam Ali @ Md. Islam vs. Amal Chandra Mondal and another. 45 DLR (AD) 27 and held that in the present case, the appellant had induced the complaint by false representation in delivering the steel grills etc. 

 6. Mr Rafique-ul-Huq, learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, submits that the first complaint having been dismissed for non-appearance of the complainant on 20-10-86 the appellant was acquitted under section 247 Cr P.C. The lodging of the second complaint on the self-same allegations was barred under section 403 Cr P.C as well as under Article 35(2) of the Constitution. Mr Huq further submits that the second petition of complaint and the complainant's statements recorded under section 200 Cr P.C on the face of it having not disclosed any initial intention of cheating to attract an offence under section 420 Penal Code, the learned Judges of the High Court Division committed an error in law in passing the impugned judgment refusing to quash the proceeding in question against the appellant. Mr. Huq also submits that the learned Judges of the High Court Division have misconstrued the principles of law enunciated in the case reported in 45 DLR (AD) 27 and thereby misdirected themselves in drawing a wrong analogy that the said reported case does not help the appellant. 

 8. As regards the first point raised by Mr Huq, namely, that section 403 Cr P.C has created a legal bar in entertaining the second petition of complaint, it is seen that the appellant was acquitted under section 247 Cr P.C on 20-10-86 on non-appearance of the complainant respondent No.2 in Criminal Case No.304-C/86. Section 247 provides: 

 "247. If the summons has been issued on complaint and upon the day appointed for the appearance of the accused, or any day subsequent thereto to which the hearing may be adjourned, the complainant does not appear, the Magistrate shall, notwithstanding anything hereinbefore contained, acquit the accused unless for some reason he thinks proper to adjourn the hearing of the case to some other day: Provided that, where the complainant is a public servant and his personal attendance is not required, the Magistrate may dispense with his attendance and proceed with the case." 

 9. The, language of section 247 thus having clearly empowered the concerned Magistrate to acquit the accused for the failure of the complaint to appear in the case on the date fixed for the appearance of the accused, it cannot be said that only the order of acquittal passed upon holding full trial can create a bar under section 403 Cr P.C from entertaining a second complaint on the self same allegation. So long as the order of acquittal, passed under section 247 Cr P.C, remains in force the provision of section 403 Cr P.C shall stand on the way of entertaining a second complaint on the self same allegations. Having gone through the impugned petition of complaint and the statements recorded thereunder by the concerned Magistrate under section 200 CrPC we cannot but hold that the alleged transaction in between the complainant and the appellant is clearly and admittedly a business transaction. The appellant had already paid a part of the money under the contract to the complainant. The failure on the part of the appellant to pay the complainant the balance amount under the bill, does not warrant any criminal proceeding as the obligation under the contract is of civil nature. The learned Judges of the High Court Division were not justified in holding that the petition of complaints having disclosed an initial element of cheating, the case in question can not be quashed. 

 10. Moreover, the principles of law enunciated in the case Islam Ali G Md. Islam vs. Omal Chandra Mondal and another 45 DLR (AD) 7 have not been properly appreciated by the learned Judges of the High Court Division in refusing to quash the proceeding in question although the transaction in question between the parties is clearly of a civil nature. 

 For the above reasons, we find substance in this appeal. Accordingly it is allowed. The impugned judgment of the High Court Division is set aside. The complaint case in question, thus, stands quashed.
